in_hebrew.name: אַרְבֵלָה
in_hebrew.meaning: פְרוּחַ עֲבֶל, עֲבִיל, עֲבֹל, שָׂע, עֵבֶל, עֲבֶל, עֲבִיל, עָבֵל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אַרְבֵלָה (Arbela) - פְרוּחַ עֲבֶל (Fruit of the Wilderness) - עֲבִיל (Abil - a place name in Syria) - עֲבֹל (Abol - a variant of Arbela) - שָׂע (Sa - a Hebrew letter) - עֵבֶל (Evil - a negative connotation in modern Hebrew, but not in biblical context) - עֲבֶל (Avbel - a rare surname) - עֲבִיל (Abil - a place name in Syria) - עָבֵל (Avbel - a rare variant of Arbela). In biblical times, Arbela was a city in Assyria, and it symbolized fruitfulness, abundance, and fertility. In Christian tradition, Arbella is associated with spiritual growth, guidance, and protection. It represents the idea of being guided through life's challenges and emerging stronger and more fruitful.

in_greek.name: Ἀρβέλλα
in_greek.meaning: Φέρω καί τρέχω, φέρων, φέρω, καί τρέχω, φέρων καί τρέχω
in_greek.long_meaning: Ἀρβέλλα (Arbella) - Φέρω καί τρέχω (To bear and to run) - φέρων (bearing, carrying) - φέρω (to bear, to carry) - καί τρέχω (and to run) - φέρων καί τρέχω (bearing and running). In the New Testament, the concept of bearing and running is associated with spiritual perseverance and endurance. Arbella represents the idea of being strong and resilient in one's faith, just like the biblical figure of Deborah, who was a strong and courageous leader. In early Christian tradition, Arbella was a popular name among the saints, symbolizing the ideals of courage, wisdom, and spiritual strength.

in_latin.name: Arbella
in_latin.long_meaning: Arbella - Femina (woman, feminine) - virtus (virtue, moral excellence) - et fortitudo (and strength, courage). In early Christian tradition, Arbella was a name associated with female saints and martyrs, symbolizing the ideals of virtue, courage, and spiritual strength. It represents the idea of being strong and confident in one's faith, just like the biblical figure of Esther, who was a courageous and virtuous queen. Arbella is also associated with the concept of fruitfulness and abundance, as seen in the biblical city of Arbela.
